Triage: NOT a code regression — environmental ENOSPC (inotify file-watcher exhaustion).

Evidence:
1. Commit 02714453 (the failing commit cited) passed the full suite TWICE via independent gates: the implement finish gate (~22:31, 526s green run) and the pre-push hook (~23:39, push succeeded only because the pre-push full --scope full gate passed). Both preceded the 00:14 start of an orphaned sibling browser vitest.
2. All 9 'failing' tests pass in isolation: tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts (40/40) and harness-cli.test.ts passed together (43/43); a 2-file isolated run was green while the concurrent 4-file run failed.
3. Measured host inotify watches peak at ~62,005/65,536 during my isolated 4-file run; ambient alone is ~28k (orphaned browser vitest 11,001 + tce vite dev server 10,980 + AI_Hell vite 5,905).
4. The errors are 'ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached' from vite-node CLI subprocesses (spawned by the CLI tests) registering recursive watchers on the project root, which now contains 18 sibling worktrees.

Root cause: an ORPHANED process (pid 3027431, ppid=1, parent session dead, hung ~4h, no output for 2h+, holding ~11k inotify watches: 'npx vitest run --project browser') + two long-running vite dev servers. Together they consume the host watch budget; any full-suite run now trips ENOSPC in the CLI-spawn tests.

Recommended fix (operator): kill the orphaned browser vitest (pid 3027431 and its chrome children) and/or raise fs.inotify.max_user_watches (currently 65536). Then re-run the suite — it will be green (file: conflicts are environmental, unrelated to test code).
